title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
comment: 42 pages, 6 figures, 15 supplementary figures. Author's version of the article published in Science Robotics. Project page: this https URL
summary: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and producing semantic labels with associated navigation costs. An open-vocabulary segmentation module converts these labels into a dense, real-time risk map, which conditions two pre-trained RL policies responsible for agile locomotion and local navigation, effectively coupling high-level VLM reasoning with low-level physical control. Real-world experiments showed the system's ability to autonomously navigate a wide range of complex real-world environments. The robot completes kilometer-long hikes with minimal intervention, interprets signs to avoid danger, and evaluates its environment to identify safe areas on which to step. This work represents a step toward the reliable deployment of systems in unstructured environments. However, it also underscores the challenges that remain in VLM reliability and spatial reasoning, indicating that foundational models are a crucial component but not yet a complete solution for navigation in the wild.

AI.tldr: ROAM 把互联网规模预训练的 VLM 的世界知识与仿真中用 RL 学到的运动/局部导航策略耦合起来，让腿式机器人完成公里级真实野外导航；摘要只给出定性结果，未报告任何数值指标。
AI.motivation: 真实世界环境的自主导航仍是最难的问题之一：既需要能应对多样地形的稳健低层运动控制，也需要能解读环境线索的高层推理。摘要指出，基础模型是导航的关键组成，但还不是完整解决方案。
AI.method: 输入是真实场景的视觉观测。VLM（在互联网规模数据上预训练）做常识推理与语义解读：评估风险、识别指示牌，并输出带导航代价的语义标签。一个开放词表分割模块把这些标签转成稠密的实时风险图，该风险图作为条件输入两个预训练 RL 策略——分别负责敏捷运动与局部导航。与单纯低层控制或单纯高层推理相比，变化在于用 VLM 语义代价把高层推理与低层物理控制连接起来。输出是机器人可执行的导航行为（运动与局部路径选择）。

title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
summary: World action models (WAMs) predict how a scene will evolve and condition their actions on this predicted future. Deploying them on a robot's onboard computer calls for 4-bit weights, activations and key-value caches (W4A4KV4). Existing 4-bit quantizers for WAMs preserve the generated action, and estimate sensitivity one denoising step at a time. However, they fail to preserve the fidelity of the predicted future: once the action pathway is protected, the remaining action error enters mostly through a degraded future that none of them deliberately protects. We propose LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read. Specifically, we introduce a reader metric, which measures future error by its effect on the action, and a read count, which weights each rounding error by the number of denoising steps that read it. Together they give the allocation of precision over activations and caches a closed-form solution. We further develop gaze-guided refinement, which gives the tokens the action attends to a second 4-bit pass in the denoising loop and in the cache. All weights stay at 4 bits, with no high-precision branch and no per-task recalibration. On the LIBERO-Plus benchmark, LAQ reaches 76.4% and 83.3% average success on Fast-WAM and Cosmos-Policy, within 1.2 percentage points of the 16-bit models and all above the baselines with 16-bit KV caches. It compresses the model by 3.8x, reduces the peak GPU memory of the whole policy by 2.3x, and runs 1.66x faster than the 16-bit model. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, it reaches 47.0% average success over three tasks, against 52.0% for the 16-bit model and 30.0% higher than QuaRot.

AI.tldr: 世界动作模型（WAM）要上机器人机载计算机需 W4A4KV4 量化，但现有 4-bit 量化器只保住生成动作、不保护预测未来；LAQ 用 reader metric 与 read count 求得精度分配的闭式解，并用 gaze-guided refinement 二次量化动作关注的 token。LIBERO-Plus 上平均成功率 76.4%（Fast-WAM）与 83.3%（Cosmos-Policy），压缩 3.8x。
AI.motivation: WAM 先预测场景如何演化，再把动作条件于该预测未来；部署到机器人机载计算机需要 4-bit 权重、激活与 KV 缓存。现有 4-bit 量化器保留生成的动作，并逐个去噪步估计敏感度，但不保护预测未来的保真度：一旦动作通路被保护，剩余的动作误差主要经由一个退化的、无人刻意保护的未来进入。
AI.method: 输入是预测场景演化并据此条件化动作的 WAM，目标是得到 W4A4KV4 的量化策略。LAQ 引入 reader metric：用未来误差对动作的影响来度量该误差；再引入 read count：按读取该舍入误差的去噪步数对其加权。两者合起来为激活与缓存的精度分配给出闭式解。另加 gaze-guided refinement：让动作所关注的 token 在去噪循环中与缓存中获得第二次 4-bit 通过。全部权重保持 4 bit，没有高精度分支，也不需要逐任务重校准。输出是量化后的 WAM 策略（含压缩后的模型与其动作预测）。
AI.result: LIBERO-Plus 上，LAQ 在 Fast-WAM 与 Cosmos-Policy 上取得 76.4% 与 83.3% 平均成功率，距 16-bit 模型 1.2 个百分点以内，且均高于使用 16-bit KV 缓存的基线。效率方面，模型压缩 3.8x，整条策略的峰值 GPU 显存降低 2.3x，相比 16-bit 模型运行快 1.66x。真机 AgileX PiPER 机械臂上，三个任务平均成功率 47.0%，16-bit 模型为 52.0%，比 QuaRot 高 30.0%。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能部署而言，该工作提示：世界动作模型量化的瓶颈可能不在动作头本身，而在被动作条件化依赖的预测未来潜变量；把量化精度按"被读取的去噪步数"和"对动作的影响"分配，可以在保持 4-bit 权重、无高精度分支、无逐任务重校准的前提下接近 16-bit 精度，并带来显存与速度收益。证据边界：结论仅来自摘要所述的 LIBERO-Plus 仿真基准与一台 AgileX PiPER 真机三任务，作者未报告统计显著性、消融或失败模式。
AI.core_method: 用"未来误差对动作的影响"（reader metric）与"读取该误差的去噪步数"（read count）推导激活与缓存的精度分配闭式解，并对动作关注的 token 做第二次 4-bit 量化。

title: GEMS: Generation and Experience Memory for Subgoal-Guided Long-Horizon World Model Planning
summary: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation. However, extending this approach to long-horizon tasks is challenging: prediction errors accumulate over extended rollouts, while latent-space similarity to distant goals provides limited guidance for ranking candidate outcomes. Existing methods address these limitations by introducing intermediate subgoals, either generated by learned models or selected from experience memory. Generated subgoals can contain hallucinations or be inaccurate in aspects such as object positions and timing. Memory-based approaches are constrained by experience coverage and may lack precise guidance for selecting appropriate intermediate states from stored observations. We introduce GEMS, which generates temporally structured subgoals to guide action search and state selection from Latent Experience Memory (LEM). A distance gate determines whether predicted outcomes are evaluated against the generated subgoal or the selected memory state. Experiments across six tasks and task suites spanning manipulation, navigation, and reaching demonstrate the effectiveness of GEMS for long-horizon planning. GEMS outperforms state-of-the-art world-model planning baselines across different manipulation settings, achieving success rates of 92.8% on Cube, 68.4% on Push-T, and 54.1% on Meta-World. It improves over the strongest evaluated baseline on these tasks by 24.0, 7.3, and 22.2 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate that generated subgoals and experience memory can jointly strengthen long-horizon planning with a frozen world model.

AI.tldr: 视觉世界模型擅长短时域目标条件规划，但长时域下预测误差累积、且与远端目标的隐空间相似度难以用于排序候选结果。GEMS 用时序结构化的生成子目标来引导动作搜索，并从隐经验记忆（LEM）中选择状态，再由距离门决定用生成子目标还是记忆状态来评估预测结果。作者报告在六个任务与任务套件上有效，并在操作类任务上超过最强基线 24.0、7.3、22.2 个百分点。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：把世界模型式规划推广到长时域很困难，一是长 rollout 中预测误差会累积，二是候选结果与遥远目标之间的隐空间相似度只能提供有限指导。已有做法引入中间子目标，但生成式子目标可能包含幻觉或在物体位置、时序等方面不准确；基于记忆的方法则受经验覆盖范围限制，从存储观测中挑选合适中间状态时可能缺乏精确指导。
AI.method: 输入是世界模型的前向预测候选结果、目标表示与隐经验记忆（LEM）中的存储观测。GEMS 生成“时序结构化”的子目标，用它来引导动作搜索，同时也用于从 LEM 中做状态选择；一个距离门（distance gate）判定每个预测结果是应对照生成的子目标评估，还是对照所选记忆状态评估。相对摘要所述基线（纯生成子目标或纯记忆子目标），变化在于把两类子目标来源放到同一规划回路中，并用距离门在两者之间切换判断依据。输出是被排序/选中的动作或状态序列以推进长时域任务，且世界模型保持冻结（frozen），方法不学习或微调世界模型本身。
AI.result: 作者报告：在跨操作、导航与到达的六个任务及任务套件上进行实验，证明 GEMS 对长时域规划有效。在操作类设置上，GEMS 超过当时的最强世界模型规划基线：Cube 成功率 92.8%、Push-T 68.4%、Meta-World 54.1%，对应分别提升 24.0、7.3、22.2 个百分点（percentage points，非相对百分比）。摘要未给出导航与到达类的数值结果，也未报告所用仿真或真实机器人平台、基线名称、样本量与统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究的含义是：在保持世界模型冻结的前提下，把“生成式子目标”与“经验记忆状态”联合起来，并用距离门按预测距离切换评估目标，可能比单独用其中一种更能支撑长时域规划。证据边界：上述收益均为作者自报、且集中在操作类任务的成功率指标上，摘要未报告真实机器人验证、运行效率或消融结果，因此不能推断该机制在真实系统或任意长时域任务上的通用性。
AI.core_method: 生成时序结构化子目标引导动作搜索，并结合隐经验记忆做状态选择，由距离门决定预测结果对照哪个子目标评估。

key_results.finding: 在操作类设置上，GEMS 成功率分别为 Cube 92.8%、Push-T 68.4%、Meta-World 54.1%，超过当时最强的世界模型规划基线。

title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
summary: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.

AI.tldr: MAWAM 把"多机器人协同操作"建模为联合预测：单次采样同时生成每个机器人的未来视角与可执行动作块。作者报告其在三个真机任务上成功率最高（平均 67.8%），并在仿真八任务上达到 90.3% 平均成功率。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出的问题是：机器人队伍中任一成员的动作都会改变队友所处的世界，因此协同操作需要把"队伍的动作"与"这些动作共同造成的物理未来"一起预测，而单机器人式的预测无法覆盖这种相互影响。
AI.method: 输入：多机器人队伍的观测与各机器人控制接口（摘要未报告具体传感器配置）。做法：以预训练的单机器人 world-action 骨干为基础，通过跨智能体注意力（cross-agent attention）对所有机器人的动作 token 与未来视角 token 做联合去噪，同时为每个机器人保留独立的控制接口。输出：单次采样即得到每个机器人的未来视角与可执行动作块（executable action chunks）。相比基线的改动在于从单机器人预测扩展为多机器人联合生成，训练中还加入 team-stage 未来视频监督。
AI.result: 真机：作者报告在 laundry-bag collection、bath-towel folding、umbrella handover 三个任务上成功率均为最高，平均 67.8%，比在同一批演示与相机上训练的 MA-VLA 高 18.9 个百分点（作者报告，未独立验证）。仿真：八个任务、最多四臂队伍下平均成功率 90.3%。消融：去掉跨智能体注意力，四臂 relay 从 95.0% 降到 39.0%；去掉 team-stage 未来视频监督，Place Food 从 78.0% 降到 47.0%。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型研究的意义在于：把世界模型预测从单机器人扩展到"队伍级"的联合动作—未来视角生成，并用消融指出跨智能体注意力与未来视频监督是协同控制的关键部件。证据边界：以上均为作者自述结果，真机任务数、真机队伍规模、演示数量、推理延迟与统计显著性摘要均未报告；仿真与真机结果不可互相外推。

title: MoRE: Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Physics Robotic World Models
summary: A robotic world model should predict how objects evolve under robot actions and physical dynamics. While recent 3D world models have shown strong predictive capabilities, they still struggle with the heterogeneous dynamics arising from diverse object interactions. To address this in a unified framework, we decompose robotic interactions into distinct physical regimes and assign each to a specialized motion expert. We introduce MoRE, a 3D world model with a mixture of motion experts organized around rigid, deformable, and prehensile dynamics. This design enables a single model to capture diverse physical behaviors while preserving regime-specific priors. Trained on mixed simulation and real-world data, MoRE integrates with Model Predictive Control (MPC) to support diverse manipulation tasks. Experiments show that MoRE improves prediction accuracy across physics regimes, leading to stronger real-world MPC performance. Code, data, and project website are available at this https URL .

title: Verify2Act: Critic-Guided Latent World Models for Verifying Language-Conditioned Manipulation Plans
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. We deploy the full system on a low-cost robot arm, training the world model and critic only on data generated in a digital twin. Across six language-conditioned tasks, Verify2Act reaches 83.3\% task success, compared with 61.7\% for a latent world model without our architectural changes, 53.3\% for the VLM alone, and 46.7\% for a pixel-diffusion world model. It verified every plan it executed and incurred no planning-induced failures: all of its failed episodes were caused by low-level grasp or placement slips. In simulation, Verify2Act obtains the highest five-task chain success on CALVIN among the compared baselines with 30$\times$ fewer reflective VLM calls than pixel-diffusion verification, and the highest success on cluttered nut assembly.

AI.tldr: VLM 能提出多步操作计划，却缺少"场景将如何变化"的 grounded 模型，而像素级世界模型既慢又在长时程漂移；Verify2Act 让 VLM 生成候选计划、在 DINOv2 特征空间想象 rollout，并由双头 critic 在执行前验证，作者报告六个语言条件任务达 83.3% 成功率。
AI.motivation: VLM 缺乏对场景变化的 grounded 模型；可用于检查计划的像素级世界模型速度慢，并随长时程漂移。因此需要把语义层面的动作提议与物理层面的执行前验证分开处理。
AI.method: 输入是语言指令对应的场景与 VLM 提出的候选多步操作计划。框架模块化地把"语义动作提议"和"潜空间物理验证"拆开：VLM 负责提议候选计划；潜在世界模型 V2A-WM 在 DINOv2 特征空间中为每个候选计划想象 rollout；双头 critic 对想象出的 rollout 检查时间一致性与目标是否达成；只有通过验证的内容才会被执行。V2A-WM 相对已有 flow-matching 世界模型的改动是加入 cross-attention action grounding 和因果时间历史窗口。世界模型与 critic 只用数字孪生中生成的数据训练，系统整体部署在低成本机械臂上。

title: Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies: Spatializing Latent Action Representations for Goal-Pose-Free Mobile Manipulation
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures. Project website: this https URL
summary: The success of manipulation policies is closely tied to the spatial relationship between the robot and the target object, as well as the task being performed, making the ability to adjust the robot's pose critical for successful execution. When the robot starts away from the task, such adjustments require coordinating navigation with local manipulation. Jointly training these capabilities incurs substantial computational and data costs, while navigating toward a predefined goal pose limits the flexibility needed to adapt to task-specific manipulation requirements. To address these challenges, we propose Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies. By leveraging the hidden representations of the policy's action-generating network as dense supervision, together with a limited number of manipulation execution outcomes, we learn a spatially conditioned embedding that captures task-dependent manipulation success across candidate robot poses. From the robot's current stereo observations, this representation estimates manipulation success at unvisited poses without rolling out the manipulation policy at each location. It is further integrated into navigation policy training, while a learned handoff policy decides when to transition from navigation to manipulation, enabling the robot to move and manipulate in a unified, task-aware manner. Across eight articulated-object tasks in unseen RoboCasa kitchens, M4M achieves 47.0% mean task success, compared with 26.5% for the strongest baseline and 19.2% for direct manipulation execution, and refrigerator-closing experiments show consistent improvements across four frozen manipulation policies.

AI.tldr: M4M 用预训练操作策略的内部隐藏表征作为密集监督，学出一个「位姿—操作成功率」的空间条件嵌入，让机器人无需预先指定目标位姿即可边导航边操作；在未见过的 RoboCasa 厨房八项关节物体任务上平均成功率 47.0%，高于最强基线 26.5% 与直接执行操作的 19.2%。

AI.method: 输入是机器人当前的双目（stereo）观测，以及一个已预训练的操作策略。方法不再联合训练导航与操作，而是从预训练操作策略中「借用」监督信号：以该策略动作生成网络的隐藏表征作为密集监督，再配合有限数量的操作执行结果，学出一个空间条件嵌入（spatially conditioned embedding），用来刻画不同候选机器人位姿下、与任务相关的操作成功率。得到该嵌入后，机器人可直接从当前双目观测估计「未访问位姿」上的操作成功情况，而无需在每个位置都实际 rollout 操作策略。该表征被进一步接入导航策略的训练；同时学习一个 handoff 策略，判断何时从导航切换到操作。最终输出是统一的、任务感知的移动+操作行为，且不依赖预先给定的目标位姿。

title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning
summary: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies from demonstrations typically samples trajectory segments uniformly or relies on static offline data curation before training. However, we find that demonstration data vary sharply in supervision value across temporal windows, and that each window's value to the policy evolves substantially during training rather than being fixed or captured by raw loss alone. Motivated by this finding, we propose RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training. RefreshGrad focuses optimization on informative, learnable windows without altering the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost. Across ten LIBERO-Plus manipulation tasks, RefreshGrad boosts average success from 60.7% (Uniform) and 68.2% (FAKTUAL) to 76.1% under visual perturbations, and from 57.4% and 73.3% to 81.3% in clean scenes.

title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. AI.tldr: WEVO 用动作条件视频世界模型作为人形全身 VLA 的后训练环境，避免真机探索风险与仿真器 sim-to-real 利用问题；三个真机任务上平均成功率由 23.3% 提升至 75.0%，高于真机 RL 的 48.3%。

title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
comment: 43 pages, 10 figures, 30 tables; supplementary material included
summary: Visual world models such as DINO-WM and JEPA-WM plan with an optimizer that searches for actions whose predicted outcome has the lowest cost, its distance to a goal image. A plan can thus fail in two ways: the optimizer never tries a good action that the cost would prefer (a search failure), or the cost, computed on predictions, ranks a bad action first (a scoring failure). The two need different remedies, more search or a better model, but a planner does not record which one occurred. We tell them apart by executing the optimizer's candidates, scoring a known solution with the planner's own cost, and comparing costs on predicted and real outcomes. An error model explains when each arises and so how to use retrieved demonstration windows (DemoProp): start the search from them (a warm start) when prediction errors are small, and average them without the model when large errors make the optimizer pick overrated actions. Across four simulated environments and three world models, on short tasks whose goals the planner can represent, PushT and Wall fail mostly by search, while Metaworld and RoboCasa fail by scoring because the cost, sound on real outcomes (AUROC 0.94 on Metaworld), is at chance on predictions (0.54). The diagnosis tells which remedy pays off: a four times larger search lowers the real-outcome cost only where failures come from search (clearly for DINO-WM), and where they come from scoring, averaging the windows without the model solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 when the model chooses among them. Within PushT, degrading only the model flips which use is better, and our rule, frozen in advance, follows the flip and solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

AI.tldr: 论文区分视觉世界模型规划的两类失败：搜索失败（优化器没试到代价偏好的好动作）与打分失败（代价在预测上把坏动作排第一），前者靠加搜索、后者靠更好的模型或绕过模型。作者用执行候选并比较预测/真实代价来诊断，并据此提出误差自适应的 DemoProp。
AI.motivation: DINO-WM、JEPA-WM 这类视觉世界模型用优化器搜索使“预测结果到目标图像距离”最小的动作。规划失败可能来自搜索不足，也可能来自代价在预测上排序错误；两者需要不同补救（更多搜索 vs 更好的模型），但规划器本身不记录到底发生了哪一种。
AI.method: 输入是优化器给出的候选动作、由预测结果到目标图像距离定义的代价，以及检索到的演示窗口。诊断做法：实际执行优化器的候选，用规划器自身的代价给一个已知解打分，并比较预测结果与真实结果上的代价，从而判断是“没搜到好动作”（搜索失败）还是“代价把坏动作排第一”（打分失败）；作者给出一个误差模型解释两类失败各自何时出现。由此得到 DemoProp：预测误差小时把演示窗口当作搜索的热启动，误差大时绕过模型、直接平均这些窗口的动作。输出是失败类型的判定与对应的规划行为。
AI.result: 作者报告：在四个仿真环境和三个世界模型上，对目标可被规划器表示的短任务，PushT 与 Wall 主要失败于搜索，Metaworld 与 RoboCasa 主要失败于打分。代价对真实结果可靠（Metaworld AUROC 0.94），对预测接近随机（0.54）。搜索扩大四倍只在失败来自搜索处降低真实结果代价（DINO-WM 明显）；在打分失败处，不用模型直接平均演示窗口解决 168 个新 Metaworld 任务中的 127 个，由模型在窗口中选择最多解决 87 个。PushT 中仅退化模型即翻转哪种用法更优，预先冻结的规则跟随该翻转，解决 960 个新 episode 中的 678 个，最佳固定用法为 530。以上均为作者报告，未经独立验证。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能中的世界模型规划，先诊断失败来源、再选择补救手段（加搜索还是改模型/绕过模型），比固定采用一种策略更有依据；DemoProp 用预测误差大小作为切换信号。证据边界：全部来自四个仿真环境、三个世界模型上的短任务，且限定于目标能被规划器表示的情形；摘要未报告真实机器人部署、长时程任务或统计显著性。
AI.core_method: 通过实际执行优化器候选并对比“预测代价”与“真实结果代价”来判定是搜索失败还是打分失败，再按预测误差大小自适应地热启动搜索或直接平均演示窗口。

title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies
summary: Robot foundation models are increasingly adapted into task specialists to expand their embodied capabilities. Yet these capabilities remain fragmented across separate policies, and existing model-merging methods do not reliably preserve them during closed-loop execution: parameter-space alignment provides only an indirect proxy for behavior, while regression may fail to preserve behavior at states not covered by its calibration inputs. We present Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy. Across two complementary timescales, TCR collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts spanning different stages of task execution and from intermediate states within iterative action generation. To account for representation shifts introduced by merging, TCR recomputes each block's input through the already merged blocks. It then uses each expert's computation within the block to form module inputs and fits merged weights to match the experts' linear outputs. A two-pass calibration procedure further refines the merged policy using separate rollout caches while retaining the frozen specialists as teachers. The resulting model preserves the original inference graph and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training. On LIBERO, TCR merges four $\pi_{0.5}$ specialists and achieves 77.83% success across 1,200 evaluation episodes, outperforming FeatCal, RegMean, and direct weight averaging by 9.50, 24.17, and 33.00 percentage points, respectively.

AI.tldr: 针对多个机器人专家策略难以在闭环执行中可靠合并的问题，TCR 用专家 rollout 与动作生成中间状态做无梯度校准，把四个 π0.5 专家合并为单一策略，在 LIBERO 的 1,200 个评估回合上取得 77.83% 成功率。
AI.motivation: 机器人基础模型被适配成任务专家后，能力分散在多个策略中；现有模型合并方法在闭环执行时不能可靠保留这些能力：参数空间对齐只是行为的间接代理，而回归校准可能无法覆盖其校准输入之外的状态。
AI.method: 输入是各专家在任务不同执行阶段的 rollout，以及迭代动作生成过程中的中间状态。TCR 先让每个待合并块接收“已经合并块”重新计算出的输入，以补偿合并带来的表征漂移；再用各专家在该块内的计算构造模块输入，拟合合并权重去匹配专家的线性输出。随后用两份独立 rollout 缓存做两遍校准，并保留冻结专家作为教师。输出是一个保持原推理图、无需专家路由、也无需额外梯度训练的单一致策。
AI.result: 在 LIBERO 上合并四个 π0.5 专家、共 1,200 个评估回合，成功率为 77.83%；相对 FeatCal、RegMean 和直接权重平均分别高出 9.50、24.17 和 33.00 个百分点（作者报告，百分点差而非相对百分比）。摘要未报告真机实验、方差或统计检验。
AI.conclusion: 该工作把策略合并的校准点从参数空间推进到实际执行轨迹与动作生成中间状态，为把多个具身专家整合为单一可部署策略提供了无梯度、无路由的路径。证据仅限摘要中的 LIBERO 四专家结果，尚不足以判断其在真实机器人、更多专家或跨任务分布上的泛化性。

title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
summary: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $\pi_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $\pi_{0.5}$.

AI.tldr: A²-VLA 让具身智能体在仿真重建场景中把工具可供性当作可构建、可验证、可修正的假设，学到的可供性提取技能与功能区域特征被用于条件化 π0.5 策略。摘要报告仿真跨工具轨迹重定向成功率 86.1%，三个真机工具使用任务成功率比 π0.5 提升 30.7 个百分点。
AI.motivation: 不同形状的工具可能具有相似功能，但跨工具迁移操作技能需要理解工具几何与具体任务的关系并相应调整策略。作者指出的关键挑战是：发现跨不同工具、对任务完成有贡献的共同可供性，并验证这些可供性是否支持新工具完成类似工作。

title: GraF-VTA: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Vision and Temporal Logic via Graph-Based Fusion
summary: Robotic planning from visual observations and signal temporal logic (STL) requires grounding task requirements in scene evidence while adapting plans to execution feedback. We present GraF-VTA, a graph-based framework that extends Vision-TL-Action with structured task representations, causal observation history, and closed-loop trajectory generation. Bidirectional cross-attention fuses STL syntax tokens with visual features, while an optional frozen automaton embedding supplies complementary untimed task structure. A temporal pyramid preserves detailed current observations and compresses older frames to provide recent execution context. Conditioned on these features and robot state, a flow-matching model generates plans whose action prefixes are executed before replanning from refreshed observations. Across five simulation environments, the single-graph configuration achieves higher open-loop Success@$K$ than TeLoGraF and Vision-TL-Action on four environments at the reported budgets $K\geq16$. On Panda, matched-update ablations increase Success@256 from 53.91\% without observation history to 62.50\% with pyramid memory. In closed-loop Dubins evaluation, it reaches 64.06\% Success@1024, compared with 12.50\% for adapted S-MSP and 27.34\% for adapted Logic-VLA. These results support combining structured visual conditioning with observation history and replanning to improve coverage of STL-satisfying trajectories.

AI.tldr: GraF-VTA 用图结构融合 STL 语法与视觉特征，并用时间金字塔保留因果观测历史与回放式重规划，直接生成满足 STL 的轨迹。摘要报告其在五个仿真环境中开放环 Success@K 优于 TeLoGraF 与 Vision-TL-Action（四个环境、K≥16），闭环 Dubins 达 64.06% Success@1024。
AI.motivation: 从视觉观测与信号时序逻辑（STL）做机器人规划，需要既把任务要求落到场景证据上，又能依据执行反馈调整计划。摘要把这两点作为待解决的缺口，并以 Vision-TL-Action 为扩展对象。
AI.method: 输入是 STL 语法 token、视觉特征与机器人状态。框架用双向交叉注意力把 STL 语法 token 与视觉特征对齐融合；可选地加入冻结自动机嵌入，提供不带时间信息的互补任务结构；时间金字塔保留当前观测的细节、压缩较旧帧以形成近期执行上下文。在这些特征与机器人状态条件下，用 flow-matching 模型生成计划，先执行动作前缀，再用刷新后的观测重新规划，形成闭环。相对于 Vision-TL-Action，主要变化是结构化任务表示、因果观测历史与闭环轨迹生成。
AI.result: 作者在五个仿真环境中报告：单图配置在四个环境、报告预算 K≥16 下开放环 Success@K 高于 TeLoGraF 与 Vision-TL-Action。Panda 上的匹配更新量消融显示，Success@256 由无观测历史的 53.91% 升至使用金字塔记忆的 62.50%。闭环 Dubins 评测中，Success@1024 为 64.06%，对比 adapted S-MSP 的 12.50% 与 adapted Logic-VLA 的 27.34%。摘要未给出延迟、算力或统计显著性数据。
AI.conclusion: 摘要支持的说法是：把结构化视觉条件、观测历史与重规划结合起来，可提升 STL 满足轨迹的覆盖度（指标为 Success@K）。证据限于仿真环境；摘要未报告真实机器人验证，也未报告开放环中未占优的那个环境的具体数值，因此不能推断通用性。

title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
summary: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

AI.tldr: 通用机器人策略能可靠执行原子技能，却在把同一批技能组合成长时程任务时失败；CoachSI让一个冻结的现成VLM只以语言"点名下一步"，把成功的被指导轨迹用原始任务指令做后见之明重标注后微调策略（动作主干冻结），随后独立部署，在未见场景长时程任务上把无辅助成功率从47.4%提升到59.3%。
AI.motivation: 作者指出的缺口是：策略靠自身经验做自改进无法弥合长时程组合的失败，因为策略自己采集的经验仍落在它自身的分布内，只能复现它已经会做的事。作者据此提出，策略缺的不是技能，而是"下一步"。
AI.method: 输入是机器人的相机图像与策略自己产生的rollout。方法不训练新的动作模型，而是让一个冻结的、现成的视觉语言模型充当"教练"：它观看机器人，用与策略原子指令相同的格式说出下一步该做什么，并且从不输出动作。策略在这个语言子目标下执行；其中成功的被指导rollout被用原始任务指令做后见之明重标注，成为微调数据，用来微调策略（摘要称增益是在动作主干冻结的情况下获得的）。产出是一个可脱离教练、单独部署的策略。与所述基线的差别在于指导信号来自冻结VLM的语言而非人类示范或纯自采集经验。
AI.result: 在World Action Model与Vision-Language-Action模型已停滞的状态上，点名下一步把子目标完成率提升为不变原始任务指令的4.6x。微调后，未见场景长时程任务的独立成功率为59.3%，较微调前的47.4%上升；作者报告这比人类示范微调高9.8个百分点、比等数据预算下自采集成功经验微调高7.3个百分点。当教练只看到相机图像时，成功率为56.8%，高于上述两个基线。摘要未报告仿真是真机、任务套件、硬件、样本量与统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该结果指向一种把语言当作"下一步子目标接口"的策略自改进路径：分布外的指导信号由冻结VLM提供，而策略已有的原子技能负责执行，因此无需改动动作主干即可获得增益。证据边界是：全部数字均出自摘要、作者自报且未经独立验证；4.6x是"模型已停滞状态"这一特定条件下的子目标完成率倍数，不等同于整体任务成功率；59.3%与56.8%的评测场景、机器人平台与真机/仿真属性在摘要中未说明。
AI.core_method: 用冻结的现成VLM观察机器人、只用语言说出与策略原子指令同格式的"下一步"，再把成功的被指导轨迹以原始任务指令重标注后微调策略（动作主干冻结），最终独立部署。

title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

AI.tldr: CauSyncVLA 用因果隐世界模型从延迟视觉锚点与已执行状态-动作历史中恢复当前感知记忆，并用 PFWS 单步修正未执行动作段，从而在异步执行下提升动作连贯性。作者报告在 LIBERO-10 上达到 93.8% 成功率与 5.04× 推理吞吐。
AI.motivation: VLA 策略必须在视觉推理仍在运行时做出反应。把计算与执行重叠可减少等待，但会留下过期（stale）的感知记忆，并使相邻动作块彼此不衔接。摘要把这两个后果作为需要解决的问题。
AI.method: 输入包含延迟的视觉锚点、已执行的状态-动作历史，以及冻结专家的控制响应。方法不改像素预测，也不做物理状态预测，而是让因果隐世界模型直接预测“当前感知记忆”，并通过动作敏感蒸馏监督以保留冻结专家的控制响应。随后以更新后的记忆为条件，Predictive Flow Warm-Starting（PFWS）把未执行的动作时间区间对齐，做单步流场修正，且无需额外训练。输出是与真实机器人执行节奏对齐的、经过修正的动作块，由异步双系统控制器执行。
AI.result: 作者报告在 LIBERO-10 上达到 93.8% 成功率，推理吞吐为 5.04×（相对倍数，摘要未给出吞吐对比基线）。摘要未报告成功率对比基线，因此无法判断该数值相对谁提升、提升多少个百分点。作者还声称闭环鲁棒性与机器人运动平滑性得到改善，但摘要未给出相应数值或指标。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型方向而言，该工作展示了一种“隐空间世界模型 + 异步执行对齐”的路线：世界模型不必预测未来像素或物理状态，而是预测被延迟视觉拖后的当前记忆，再用该记忆修正待执行动作。证据边界是：仅有摘要级别的单一基准数值与吞吐倍数，摘要未报告基线对照、消融、统计显著性、真机实验说明，故不能推断方法的泛化性或实际部署表现。

title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
summary: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action

summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role. However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation across consecutive decisions without changing the output. title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
summary: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our code is available at this https URL .

title: WAMotor: Accelerating World Action Models via Speculative Inference under Dual Nonuniform Denoising Dynamics
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) unify world modeling and action generation for robotic control by integrating flow-matching velocities, yet suffer from high multi-step denoising latency. Recent studies have explored speculative inference to accelerate WAMs by drafting and verifying denoising steps in parallel. However, existing methods either require training task-specific draft models or overlook critical WAM denoising dynamics when reusing past velocities as drafts. We revisit the denoising dynamics of WAMs and identify a dual nonuniformity that breaks standard velocity-reuse assumptions: velocity smoothness is nonuniform as adjacent velocity residuals differ sharply at early and final steps, so reuse there yields large residuals, which nonuniform integration time steps further translate into local state errors that accumulate into the final action distribution. Accordingly, we formalize this by theoretically deriving a trajectory error tolerance bound that characterizes how velocity residuals and integration time steps affect the final action distribution. Based on this, we propose WAMotor, the first speculative inference method tailored to the dual nonuniformity in WAMs. It selects reliable anchor velocities by deferring speculation and employs time-step-aware verification that scales acceptance thresholds by integration time step size. WAMotor offers plug-and-play benefits, enabling seamless integration with prior WAMs. Extensive evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and LIBERO-Plus show that WAMotor achieves 2.86$\times$--4.28$\times$ end-to-end speedups while maintaining task success rates. Our code is available at: this https URL

title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Although existing vision--tactile--language--action (VTLA) policies incorporate tactile feedback, when and how touch refines actions under changing visual conditions remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{TipDex-VTLA}, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE) compares predicted and measured touch at matched times and combines the resulting discrepancy with visual reliability to gate bounded feature corrections for unexecuted actions. This effectively helps to refine actions under challenging unseen visual conditions. We evaluate TipDex-VTLA on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark. TipDex-VTLA trained on data collected under normal visual conditions, achieves average full-task success rates of 87.5% (resp. 73.8%) under normal (resp. challenging unseen) lighting in real-world tasks, significantly outperforming some state-of-the-art methods. We will release the collected data and source code.

title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
summary: Animals use many different gaits to locomote at different speeds across varying terrains. A longstanding question in biology and robotics is: which gait is best? This question is most often addressed from an energy-efficiency perspective on flat terrain, leaving open how the answer depends on terrain and on the criterion optimized. Here we show that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity. We use deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, together with the locomotion style (base height, foot ground clearance, foot offsets) that each requires. A second policy then selects among them to optimize a user-specified criterion such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Across these performance metrics and within this repertoire, every gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination. The framework adapts zero-shot to gait couplings and styles never seen during training, to terrains far beyond the training distribution, and to larger quadrupeds five times the training mass. With a single additional pitch-tracking reward term, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion. Our method provides a general and systematic way to produce expressive locomotion and to select the gait best suited to a given terrain and criterion. Project page: this https URL .

title: LeCompass: Task-Level Execution through State-Indexed Interfaces
summary: Action-conditioned joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) offer a foundation for predictive decision-making by modeling the consequences of actions in representation space. Yet evaluating local reachability in latent space does not by itself provide a task-level execution interface: intermediate targets must be generated, local inference has finite budgets, and execution requires spatial feedback and persistent interaction state. We introduce LeCompass, a state-indexed execution framework built around a frozen LeWorldModel (LeWM). A proposer supplies intermediate latent targets, while CompassFlow searches the source space of a learned trajectory prior to obtain effective action candidates under limited predictive-evaluation budgets. Patch-token readouts provide spatial feedback, while observation-based memory supports phase transitions and bounded recovery. State-indexed targets support cross-episode context-goal composition. On 1,000 official TEST full-episode Cube trials, the complete LeCompass execution system achieves 86.9% native 4-cm reach. Separate matched analyses show that predictive ranking raises success from 4.7% to 44.9% on TEST PushT and from 33.8% to 77.7% on TEST TwoRoom. These results demonstrate task-level execution with task-dependent roles for latent target proposal, predictive search, and observation-grounded control.

title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
summary: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations. This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79, alongside up to 23% lower FVD. These gains carry over to planning, where selecting actions with AFFECT-trained world models improves task success by up to 8.3%.

title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation
summary: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops. Each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation show better success rates and efficiency. On RoboTwin, UniVEP hits 61.36% success with one StarVLA run, beating the best single-target baseline at sixteen runs (59.96%). With LiLa-WAM, two runs outperform the best sixteen-step single-target baseline and cut inference latency by 77.1%.

AI.tldr: 论文发现 flow-matching 机器人策略中速度预测与端点预测在不同噪声阶段互补，据此提出 UniVEP：联合学习两种预测目标并随噪声下降从端点恢复切换到速度精修。摘要报告在 RoboTwin 与 LiLa-WAM 上以更少推理步数取得更高成功率，并降低 77.1% 推理延迟。

AI.method: 输入是 flow-matching 动作生成过程中的带噪动作；作者先在多个机器人策略、基准与推理预算下比较 V、X、X--V 三种预测目标，并分析不同噪声水平下二者的互补性（高噪声下端点预测更稳定，接近干净动作时速度预测校正更准）。UniVEP 在此发现上联合学习两种预测目标，加入一致性监督，并随噪声降低把生成方式从端点恢复切换为速度精修；每个生成步只需一次网络前向，输出机器人动作。

title: Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present
summary: A robot must choose an action before it can see the outcome. In a recorded demonstration, later camera frames show what happened after the robot moved. Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD) uses these later frames to teach a policy what to extract from current images. During training, a teacher sees both the current and later frames, while a student sees the current frames. They share a visual encoder and an action predictor. Each branch summarizes its images with a small set of feature vectors. These visual summaries supply all visual input to the action predictor. The teacher learns from demonstrated actions. For each noisy action sequence, the student learns from either the demonstration or the teacher's denoising prediction. It also learns to match the teacher's visual summaries. We analyze which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs. At deployment, the student encodes the current images once and reuses its summaries at every denoising step. HSD achieves average success rates of 98.50\% on LIBERO and 92.31\% on RoboTwin 2.0.

AI.tldr: 机器人必须在看到结果前选择动作；HSD 用演示中较晚的相机帧作为教师特权信息，训练仅见当前帧的学生策略，并让教师视觉摘要指导动作去噪。作者报告在 LIBERO 和 RoboTwin 2.0 上平均成功率分别为 98.50% 和 92.31%。
AI.motivation: 在录制的演示中，机器人动作之后的较晚相机帧包含动作结果；摘要指出机器人必须在看到结果前选动作，因此需要利用这些后见帧来教策略从当前图像中提取有用信息。摘要未说明与既有方法的对比缺口。

title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
summary: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. title: PhysVAM: Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
comment: 23 pages, 10 figures. Project page: this https URL
summary: Predicting future scene or object states does not necessarily reveal how robot-object interactions will advance or hinder a task. This challenge is particularly pronounced in dynamic robotic manipulation, where objects continue moving during perception and execution. Effective action generation therefore requires not only modeling object dynamics but also anticipating how future interactions will shape task progress. To this end, we propose \textbf{PhysVAM}, a Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress. This value-based formulation provides task-directed foresight without reconstructing future visual states. Conditioned on current observations and historical object and robot motion, PhysVAM jointly learns action generation and multi-horizon future-value prediction. The value branch learns horizon-specific latent representations through future task-value prediction from successful and failed trajectories. These future-value representations are integrated into the action policy through gated cross-attention, guiding action generation toward interactions that facilitate task success. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate superior task success, with absolute success-rate improvements of 27.0 and 27.5 percentage points over the strongest baselines in simulation and real-world tasks, respectively. Project page: this https URL .

title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
summary: A collision-free detour can still bring a legged robot to the next stair or ledge a few centimetres or degrees off, and a fixed locomotion skill, factory or learned, can stall or fall. Existing methods prevent this with a robot model or extensive trial and error, but on a new site with unknown skills neither is available, so they cannot be used. We find that a single 27-minute teaching session already supplies what these methods have to derive or learn: for every stair and ledge, one crossing the skill has completed. Our method, passage-conditioned navigation, makes the route remember how each transition was entered, not only where the path went. It stores each taught crossing as an event and, without training or a robot model, enforces it after every local replan: before each ledge, an entry gate makes the robot turn or back up and retry if it is more than 10 cm or 10° off the taught crossing. Under localization noise, with path, gait schedule, and sensing unchanged, this raises the share of disturbed ledge crossings that stay within these limits from 24.1% to 88.6%. In contact simulation with our learned policies, a robot pushed off course before stairs never falls in 180 climbs, against 9 falls when the stored direction is ignored; pushed 1.2 m away, it rejoins the route, ending on average 0.14 m from it (1.10 m without rejoining), and finishes as often as an undisturbed robot. This suits any robot with fixed skills that repeats a route over terrain transitions, as in inspection and patrol, where one wrong entry can end the task. We deployed it in competition on a real wheeled-legged robot: over 271 m of multi-obstacle terrain spanning 7.0 m of elevation, it completed all six runs, won third place at the 2026 Global Open-source AI Challenge, which drew 2,999 submissions, and was the only finalist in its task to finish fully autonomously.

AI.tldr: 论文针对固定步态技能在楼梯/边缘处因入位偏差而停滞或摔倒的问题，提出 passage-conditioned navigation：把 27 分钟教学中的每次跨越记录为路线事件，并在局部重规划后用入口门约束进入姿态。摘要报告定位噪声下受扰边缘通过的合规比例由 24.1% 升至 88.6%，接触仿真中楼梯前 180 次攀爬 0 次跌倒（忽略存储方向为 9 次），真机竞赛完成全部六次运行。
AI.motivation: 无碰撞绕行仍可能让腿式机器人以数厘米或数度的偏差到达下一级台阶或边缘，固定步态技能（出厂或学习所得）会因此停滞或跌倒。已有方法依赖机器人模型或大量试错，但在新场地且技能未知时两者都不可用。
AI.method: 输入是一段 27 分钟的教学过程：对每个台阶和边缘记录技能成功完成的一次跨越，以及该次跨越是如何进入的。方法把每次教学跨越存为事件，附加到路线记忆中，而不是只保存路径经过的位置。每次局部重规划后、到达边缘前，用入口门执行该事件：若机器人相对教学跨越的偏差超过 10 cm 或 10°，就转向或后退并重试。该过程不需要训练，也不需要机器人模型。输出是经入口条件约束后的路线与运动指令，使固定技能在重复路线上以一致姿态进入地形过渡。

title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency
summary: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $\pi_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.

AI.tldr: 多视图 VLA 只在机器人基座系接受动作监督，需要隐式学习"某个视角的观测↔基座系动作"的空间对应，因此对相机视角和机器人初始状态变化敏感。OVOA-VLA 改为在每个视角的相机坐标系下预测动作，让同一物理运动在不同视角产生多样且与观测对齐的监督，并用两组有向注意力图与跨图一致性把视角专家的监督汇入基座系预测。作者报告 LIBERO-Plus 上全视图与仅基座推理平均成功率 88.1% 与 85.7%，真实世界仅基座推理把 π_0.5 的 28.3% 提升到 58.3%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，多视图 VLA 模型的动作监督通常只存在于机器人基座坐标系中，模型必须自行隐式学习每个视角的观测与基座系动作之间的空间对应关系。这在相机视角变化和机器人初始状态变化时造成空间泛化困难。作者认为这种监督形式本身是缺口：同一物理运动在各视角中本可提供与观测对齐的监督，但现有做法没有利用它。
AI.method: 输入仍是同一组多视图观测（外加机器人状态）。相对基座系单一监督的基线，OVOA-VLA 让每个视角的动作专家在各自相机坐标系下接收机器人状态输入并输出该坐标系下的动作目标，即"一个视角对应一个动作"，使同一物理运动在不同视角生成多样、与观测对齐的监督信号。模型同时联合训练一个基座系专家和若干视角专属动作专家，并用两组互补的有向注意力图刻画基座专家与视角专家之间两个方向的交互，从而把视角专属的动作监督用于改进基座系预测。跨图一致性（Cross Graph Consistency）进一步约束两组图对同一样本给出的基座系预测相互一致。输出为动作；在相同多视图输入下，模型同时支持全视图推理和仅基座（base-only）推理两种模式。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于：把动作监督从单一基座坐标系扩展到"逐视角相机坐标系"，可能是一种无需改变输入模态即可获得空间泛化的监督设计思路，并通过图间一致性把多视角监督回灌到基座系策略，使部署时甚至可以只用基座系推理。证据边界：全部结论为作者自述，未独立验证；仿真结果限于 LIBERO-Plus 等基准，真实世界结果仅覆盖三个任务且只与 π_0.5 比较；摘要未提供消融、显著性、硬件或推理延迟信息，因此无法判断增益来自哪一组件，也无法判断仅基座推理在真实场景中的计算代价。

title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Code-as-policy robot-use agent post-training
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

AI.motivation: 大型多模态模型可支持长时程机器人操作，但频繁调用带来显著延迟与token成本；核心难点是判断何时需要agent协助或介入，以及错误应修复机器人执行、子任务规划，还是两者。摘要未报告具体延迟或成本数值。
AI.method: 输入包括低层策略的例行执行、时序视觉观测与有序交互记忆。在线任务状态监视器融合视觉与记忆，联合估计当前子任务进度并预测后继子任务；预测触发事件驱动的agent审查，协调执行修复与计划修订。经核实的结果用于更新记忆与子任务切换，使常规执行仍由低层策略承担，推理只用于需要额外评估的决策。相对所述基线，关键改变是把高层推理调用从常态改为事件触发。

title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

AI.tldr: UniCraft 通过统一坐标约定与感知/控制接口、把跨基准任务改写成规范格式，让 3 个基准、6 种本体的交互经验共同训练一套共享技能与调度策略；作者报告在未见场景上任务成功率提升 9–28 个百分点（LIBERO-PRO）等，并在训练后冻结技能实现对新本体与新模型的零样本迁移。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出 VLM 在任务与领域间泛化较好，但机器人操作的同类泛化仍困难：本体、任务表述、几何约定与动作接口的异质性，把交互经验割裂在不同基准与硬件上。作者因此提问：跨基准、跨本体的异构交互能否共同改进同一套操作技能。
AI.method: 输入是多个基准、多种机器人上的交互数据（抽象表述为"观察到的场景几何"与交互反馈）。方法做的是对齐而非微调：用一致的坐标约定表示场景几何，对齐不同机器人的感知与控制接口，并把不同基准的任务整理为规范格式。这样交互反馈可以同时更新共享技能库，以及决定技能如何选择与组合的调度策略（orchestration policy）。输出是共享技能加调度策略组成的操作智能体；摘要强调过程不使用示范数据、也不更新模型权重。
AI.result: 作者报告：在 3 个基准、6 种本体上交错训练、每个智能体模型采集 2,700 条学习 rollout 后，训练期间在未见场景与任务上的汇总任务成功率提升 9–28 个百分点（LIBERO-PRO）、10.8–13.3（RoboTwin 2.0）、3.1–14.4（RoboCasa365，Epochs 1–3）。训练后冻结已学技能，在 robosuite 与 RoboDojo 上实现对 4 种新机器人本体与 5 个额外智能体模型的零样本迁移。摘要未给出绝对成功率数值、具体对照基线定义，也未说明是仿真还是真机结果。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与跨本体技能复用研究而言，该工作把"经验复用"问题定位为表示与接口对齐问题，而非单纯扩充数据或加大模型；其证据支持的是：在对齐之后，多基准多本体的异构交互能共同提升未见场景下的任务成功率，且技能可在冻结状态下迁移到新本体与新智能体模型。限制在于摘要只给出百分点提升区间、未给出绝对成功率、基线细节与仿真/真机条件，且各提升为作者自报、未经独立验证。

title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
comment: A two-stage pipeline that teaches VLAs to stop prohibited tasks safely while preserving permitted skills
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.

AI.tldr: SAFI 面向 VLA 执行中途的安全停止：在禁止任务示范中构造静止手臂命令与一致夹爪目标的“保持”替代响应，并与保留任务动作联合训练，使策略在中间执行状态显式回退。作者报告在 OpenVLA-OFT、LIBERO 与 BadLIBERO 任务上，接管后聚合目标成功率降至 1.3\%，无记录的物理事故或动作饱和，并保持高保留任务成功率。
AI.motivation: 已有工作探索任务抑制与拒绝，但执行中途停止被禁行为并控制物理响应仍困难；评估显示从初始状态抑制任务的策略在接管后仍可能完成任务，且即使任务未完成也可能掉落所持物体，因此“未完成”不足以衡量安全。
AI.method: 输入是视觉观察、语言指令以及执行中途的机器人状态。SAFI 分两阶段改变策略：第一阶段在禁止任务示范中构造回退目标，把手臂命令设为静止并给夹爪一致目标；第二阶段做联合策略适配，让策略同时学习这些回退目标和保留任务的原动作。输出是能在中间执行状态显式切换到“保持/停止”替代响应、同时维持其他技能的 VLA 策略。相对于从初始状态抑制任务的基线，关键变化是从一开始就学习中间状态的显式替代行为，而不是只让被禁任务不完成。
AI.result: 作者在 OpenVLA-OFT 上跨 LIBERO 与 BadLIBERO 任务评估被禁任务完成、物理事故与保留任务性能。在评估的 LIBERO 任务上，作者报告 SAFI 将接管后聚合目标成功率降至 1.3\%，无记录的物理事故或动作饱和，并保持高保留任务成功率。摘要未报告基线具体数值、保留任务成功率具体值、样本量、统计显著性、真实机器人或硬件条件；由于没有基线数值，也不能计算相对百分比或百分点改进。
AI.conclusion: 这说明 VLA 安全停止可能需要针对中间执行状态的显式替代响应监督，而不仅是初始状态的任务拒绝/抑制。证据边界是：结论仅来自摘要中 OpenVLA-OFT 在 LIBERO 与 BadLIBERO 任务的作者报告，且摘要未报告真实机器人部署、硬件细节、样本量、统计显著性或基线数值，不能据此推断广泛场景的部署安全性。
AI.core_method: SAFI 通过在禁止任务示范中构造静止手臂与固定夹爪的回退目标，并与保留任务动作联合训练，让 VLA 在中间执行状态学会显式切换到保持/停止响应。

Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety.

title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

AI.tldr: 现有视触觉 VLA 加入触觉输入收益不稳定，因为多数触觉变化（如夹爪闭合时的凝胶形变）可由视觉与已执行动作预测。TacInno 只把"视觉与动作无法解释的接触动力学"（触觉 innovation）作为训练目标：先把它压成离散码，再让策略预测该码，部署时不新增对应模块。作者报告在 6 个仿真任务上平均成功率 87.5%、4 个真实任务 70.5%，分别比最强视触觉基线高 10.7 和 9.0 个百分点。
AI.motivation: VLA 模型被加入触觉感知以捕捉视觉上不明显的接触事件，但摘要指出：加入触觉输入带来的增益不一致，某些视触觉 VLA 模型几乎不依赖触觉输入。原因是大量触觉变化（例如夹爪闭合过程中的凝胶形变）可以从视觉观测和执行动作中预测出来，这类"可预测"的触觉信号对策略没有额外信息量。
AI.method: 输入为视觉观测、已执行动作以及未来的触觉变化。方法先定义"tactile innovation"——视觉观测与已执行动作无法解释的那部分接触动力学；TacInno tokenizer 以视觉观测和已执行动作为条件，把未来触觉变化压缩为一个离散码；策略 TacInno-VLA 学习预测该码，即把该码当作辅助训练目标。与直接以触觉输入作为策略输入的基线相比，变化点在于监督对象被换成"残差式"触觉信号，且部署时不增加用于该码的模块。输出是一个用于接触丰富操作的策略。
AI.result: 作者报告（未经独立验证）：6 个仿真任务平均成功率 87.5%，4 个真实世界任务平均成功率 70.5%；相对最强的视触觉基线分别高出 10.7 和 9.0 个百分点（percentage points，非相对百分比）。摘要称消融研究验证了视觉与动作条件、多帧编码、辅助码预测三者的贡献，但未给出消融数值。作者未在摘要中给出具体基准名称与基线方法名。

title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
summary: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $\pi_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

title: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models
comment: 24 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Robotic world models predict future video frames from the current observation and a sequence of robot actions. While recent models follow the given actions closely, manipulated objects often collapse or move inconsistently with the action. We attribute this to the conditioning: an action, or a rendering of the robot, specifies where the robot goes but not how the scene responds, leaving a single video model to infer the interaction dynamics implicitly while also rendering appearance. We therefore separate dynamics prediction from visual rendering, with 3D point dynamics as the proxy between them. Specifically, we lift the first frame into 3D points, simulate how they respond to the robot's motion with a learned point dynamics model, and render the simulated points back into pixel-aligned videos that any video model can read. In controlled experiments on the DROID dataset with two video renderers of different architectures, this point dynamics proxy reduces object motion error by 8.6% and 6.2% without degrading image quality, and by 8.1% on a real bimanual robot. Moreover, the video follows the simulation: more accurate dynamics yield more accurate object motion, and editing the points steers the video. This suggests that advances in dynamics modeling can translate into more faithful robotic world models.

AI.tldr: 机器人世界模型常能跟随动作却让被操作物体崩塌或运动不一致，作者将其归因于动作条件只交代机器人去哪、未交代场景如何响应。方法把动力学预测与视觉渲染分开，用3D点动力学作为中间代理，在DROID数据集与真实双臂机器人上降低了物体运动误差。

title: Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies
summary: Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output. We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $\pi_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network. The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers. On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points. The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]). Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%. High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.

AI.tldr: 论文重新检验flow-based VLA策略中首尾动作token的“radial action sink”解释：在单个π0.5检查点上，高注意力质量并未伴随小值、低影响的端点token，RoPE造成注意力集中，而前缀BOS更符合sink特征。作者进一步报告，用其他任务估计的相对偏移路由可维持闭环成功率（42.7%对38.7%），但证据限于五个RoboCasa任务。
AI.motivation: 已有工作把flow-based VLA策略首尾动作token上的高注意力称为radial action sink，并据此设定执行时域；但语言模型中sink还应具有小value和低输出影响，这一profile是否成立尚未被检验。摘要明确只检验该profile，不检验horizon rule。
AI.method: 输入是单个π0.5检查点在五个RoboCasa任务上的动作token注意力与value；作者不训练新策略，而是在18层上比较首尾token与普通动作token的key质量、value范数，并分析RoPE来源，再用遮蔽、置零和跨观测值方向替换做因果测试，以250个配对回合的成功率衡量影响。随后在动作块内测试一个在其他任务上估计的相对偏移路由profile，并在三个held-out任务上测闭环成功率；摘要未报告该路由的具体实现细节。

title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
summary: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.

AI.tldr: LoopedWAM 用循环共享的六块核心替代庞大视频/动作 Transformer，让每个专家以 12 块的存储执行 30 层计算；0.58B 策略参数、无机器人预训练下在 LIBERO 达 96.1%，并以弹性自蒸馏给出单一 checkpoint 的多个精度-延迟工作点。
AI.motivation: 世界动作模型（WAM）把生成式视频建模与机器人动作预测耦合，但摘要指出这类模型通常需要大型视频与动作 Transformer，限制部署效率。作者要解决的是这一部署效率瓶颈，而非建模能力本身。
AI.method: 输入是查询（视觉输入）与机器人动作预测任务。方法在每个专家内部循环复用同一个六块核心，从而以 12 块的存储量执行 30 层 Transformer 计算。由于视频与动作专家推理代价不对称——视觉特征每个查询只算一次，动作计算则在每个采样步重复——两者被允许使用不同深度。此外提出弹性自蒸馏，用一份权重训练出单个弹性 checkpoint（LoopedWAM-E），覆盖不同的动作深度与采样步预算。输出是动作预测，以及可由同一 checkpoint 选择的多档精度-延迟工作点。
